implementation_notes:
Turn 1 had already placed the single count node above the list, but worded it `${count} notes` for every count and had the suite pin "1 notes". That contradicts the delivered spec (features/note-count-header/note-count-header.feature: 'The count label shows a single note' -> reads "1 note"; ASSUM-004 in feature_spec_inputs/27896ec8-...md: "'3 notes', '1 note', '0 notes'") and AC-003. This turn corrected the wording to the specified singular/plural rule and re-anchored the tests to it. 1. apps/web/src/App.tsx:18-20 - noteCountLabel(count) now returns `${count} ${count === 1 ? 'note' : 'notes'}`, exactly the format the implementation notes prescribe. It is the only place in the web app that renders a notes total (grep for noteCountLabel / notes-count returns one call site, App.tsx:131), so the label is not duplicated. It sits as `

` immediately before `

    ` (App.tsx:131-132), outside the list, and is rendered unconditionally - including at zero. Its text is computed from `count = notes.length` (App.tsx:32), the same value the tab title effect reads (`Notes (${count})`, App.tsx:57), and `notes` is the state populated only by the client-side `listNotes` response (App.tsx:34-51) that the `
      ` maps over, so label, tab title and rows can never drift. 2. apps/web/src/App.test.tsx - reused the existing shape helpers untouched (totalAboveTheList at :441-451, notesList at :413-420, totals at :422-427, documentOrder, noteRows). Changes: the shared `countLabel` wording helper now encodes the singular rule; the `it.each([0,1,5,12,37])` collection-size case asserts `countLabel(notes.length)` instead of hard-coding the plural; the wording table reads [1, "1 note"]; the shape case was re-pinned from `/^\d+ notes$/` to `/^\d+ notes?$/` plus `countLabel(size)` plus digit-vs-rows equality; the two single-note expectations now read "1 note"; and a new explicit `it.each([[0, "0 notes"], [1, "1 note"], [100, "100 notes"]])` case states the three AC-003 values by name as exact text (not just a pattern), each also asserting the row count matches. 3. Scope: `git diff --stat HEAD` shows only apps/web/src/App.tsx and apps/web/src/App.test.tsx. Nothing under apps/api/, contract/ or tests/ was touched. Deliberate non-change: the pre-existing browser check tests/e2e/specs/journey.spec.ts (authored for TASK-NLTC-001) reads this label as `/^\d+ notes$/` and `${expected} notes`, so it would disagree with the spec's "1 note" at a count of one. AC-005 forbids editing tests/, and the ACs plus the feature file are the contract for this task, so the web app follows the spec and the drift is reported under `concerns` rather than fixed here. That spec is not part of the registered producers: scripts/check.sh only typechecks and prettier-formats tests/e2e; the Playwright run lives in scripts/check-feature.sh behind the live-gate driver and needs the Keycloak/Postgres stack.
concerns: Pre-existing contract drift, out of this task's scope: tests/e2e/specs/journey.spec.ts:51-52 asserts the summary text as `${expected} notes` and /^\d+ notes$/ (plural-only) for every count it walks through, including `seeded + 1`, i.e. a count of one. Under the spec-correct "1 note" wording that live-gate check would fail at exactly one note. It cannot be reconciled inside this task because AC-005 forbids any change under tests/. It is owned by the TASK-NLTC-001 journey artifact / the live-gate flow (scripts/check-feature.sh), not by TASK-15DD-001, and it is not run by the registered `test` producer (bash scripts/check.sh). Recommend the reviewer route the regex update to that owner.

The label is static at initial render for this iteration (per the implementation notes: dynamic add/remove updates are out of scope), although the existing tests 'follows the collection when the view itself adds a note' and the tab-title add/removal cases already demonstrate it re-derives from the same collection on re-render.

completion_promises.evidence: This is what turn 1 got wrong and turn 2 fixed. apps/web/src/App.tsx:18-20 now returns `${count} ${count === 1 ? "note" : "notes"}`, so 1 reads "1 note" while 0/2/100 read "0 notes"/"2 notes"/"100 notes". The label is rendered unconditionally (no `count > 0 &&` guard), so zero stays visible. New test coverage: an explicit `it.each([[0, "0 notes"], [1, "1 note"], [100, "100 notes"]])` case ('states the count for %i as the single total %s') asserting exact text plus row-count agreement; the 'keeps the zero total visible above an empty list' case asserting totals(container) has length 1 and the text is "0 notes" over an empty collection; the wording table entry corrected to [1, "1 note"]; the two single-note placement/tab-title cases corrected to "1 note"; and the shape case re-pinned to /^\d+ notes?$/ with countLabel(size) for [0,1,2,3,5,12,100]. vitest reports all three new named cases passing (0 notes, 1 note, 100 notes).
